captures.description: THE FILE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Virtual International Authority File (VIAF) is an international name authority service that combines multiple national library authority files into a single online database.' Key Features: operator (OCLC); origin (1998, Library of Congress, DNB, OCLC; 'launching formally in August 2003'); purpose ('linking variant names, pseudonyms, and corporate titles'); integration ('Each cluster receives a unique standard identifier/URI'); access. Six cards: VIAF, OCLC (two), Wikipedia, the LOD Cloud, the Semantic Web Journal.

atoms.evidence: is an international name authority service that combines multiple national library authority files into a single online database.
Operator: Hosted and maintained by OCLC (Online Computer Library Center).
Origin: Initiated in 1998 as a joint proof-of-concept by the U.S. Library of Congress, the German National Library (DNB), and OCLC, launching formally in August 2003.
